title: Async all the way
sub: How to really cure a deadlock
cards/0/body:
If the code inside is asynchronous, the code outside should await too, all the way up to the event handler or Main. That's async all the way.

Mixing them with .Result and .Wait() is called sync-over-async: it gives you both deadlocks and pool starvation.
cards/1/task: Fix the deadlock properly: no ConfigureAwait, just make the handler async.
cards/2/q: Why is await better than .Result in a handler?
cards/2/options/0: The UI thread doesn't block: continuations and clicks keep running, so a deadlock is impossible
cards/2/explain: No blocked thread, no wait cycle.
cards/3/body: Since C# 7.1, Main can be async Task Main(). Event handlers are async void: the one sensible place for void. ASP.NET Core controllers return Task<IActionResult>.
cards/4/explain: .Result holds a pool thread for the whole database query.
cards/5/explain: async in the declaration, await before the call.
cards/6/body:
Wrapping a synchronous blocking call in Task.Run and naming the method …Async is a trick: a thread is still busy, just a different one.

Don't do this in a library: let the caller decide whether they need Task.Run.
cards/7/q: Which of these are sync-over-async? Select all that apply.
cards/7/explain: Any synchronous wait on a task blocks the thread.
